The ward reads state admitted, WARD-C, version 2, epoch 10. Version 2 was set by BEDMGR transfer MSG00803 to WARD-C with the same event_time 08:20:00Z. The route supports conditional writes, receipts and dry runs, so a resend against version 2 would go through: it would move the patient from WARD-C to WARD-B and overwrite the bed manager's placement (E7). By inference only (DEP-1.1), that would change the bed board, redirect pharmacy and create a porter task (DEP-2.2 if BEDMGR is the correct placement). Reconcile does not fit, because no receipt exists and the PAS movement is not in effect. Superseded is not established, because the BEDMGR event is not strictly later. Doing nothing leaves WARD-C in place. That is correct if BEDMGR is authoritative; if PAS is, the patient stays recorded on the wrong ward (DEP-2.3). Which outcome is right cannot be bounded from here, so this needs a human decision.

# Impact Analysis specialist

Work out the effect of each option: a resend applies one movement conditional on the receiver's version (it fails safely when the version moved); a reconciliation records a committed movement and changes nothing at the receiver; doing nothing leaves the receiver as it is. Say which effects Shutter can verify afterwards (the receipt and the history) and which it cannot (consumers downstream).

   - resend when the effect is one bounded movement, the receiver supports conditional writes and dry runs, and the receiver's state shows it would apply;

   - superseded when a later applied event means a resend would move the record backwards;
   - escalate when the receiver cannot guard the write (no conditional writes) or the effect cannot be bounded;
   - more_evidence when the capability profile or the receiver's state could not be read.
